AddPersonRequest.description:
`POST /v1/people`: add a person. Only an admin may. They sign in with
the password, with Google by the email, or with either: one of the two is
needed, and the email alone only where the server signs people in with
Google.

email.description: The address of the Google account they sign in with.

AddTokenRequest.description: `POST /v1/tokens`: make a token. Only an admin may.

name.description:
What its changes are recorded under, as `agent:<name>`: 1 to 64
letters, digits, `.`, `_` or `-`. No other token has it.

AddedToken.description:
A token that was just made. This is the only time the server says what
the token is: it keeps a hash of it.

Authored.description: A changeset the engine wrote for a caller, and its receipt.

committed.description:
`None` when the caller asked only to see the changeset. It was
validated all the same.

Candidate.description: An identity that the records of a review item matched.

members.description:
Its members: those a judgement of the case names before the others,
and at most [`CASE_MEMBERS`] of them. `identity.members` says how
many there are.

CandidateList.description:
`GET /v1/runs/{run}/candidates` when JSON is asked for. Each candidate has
`left_id`, `right_id`, and every feature column prefixed with `left_` and
with `right_`.

CaseConstraint.description: A constraint in force, with where its two records are.

from.description: The log position of the changeset that made it.

identities.description:
The identities its records belong to now, that of `a` first.
`None` for one that has no identity.

ChangePersonRequest.description:
`POST /v1/people/{id}`: change a person. Only an admin may. A field left
out stays as it is. A new password, or turning the account off, signs
the person out everywhere. Another email signs them out wherever they
signed in with Google.

email.description:
The address of the Google account they sign in with. An empty one
takes it away, for someone who has a password.

Changeset.description: An ordered list of operations that is applied atomically or not at all.

base.description: The log position the author had seen.

run.description: The reconcile run that drafted it, if any.

ChangesetId.description: Identifies a changeset, and the draft it was while it waited.

head.description: The position of the last committed changeset.

CommitRequest.description:
`POST /v1/changesets`: a changeset to validate and commit. Its author is
whoever sends it: the person signed in, or the agent whose token it is.

A caller that has read the state it is changing says so with `base`: a
merge is rejected if the members of either identity changed after it. A
caller that leaves `base` out is taken to have read the head of the log.

base.description: The log position the author had read. Left out, the head of the log.

id.description:
The changeset's ID. Left out, the server mints one. A caller that may
send the same changeset twice mints the ID itself, so that the second
one is refused.

Committed.description: The receipt for a committed changeset.

Comparison.description: What one match run made of a pair.

blocked_by.description:
The block rules that made the pair a candidate in this run. Empty
when a strategy judged a pair no block rule had found.

draft.description:
When the run's draft was left for review: what became of it. Of a
run that was reconciled more than once, the latest draft.

judgements.description:
What the strategy judged. Empty when the pair was a candidate and
got no judgement.

ConstraintEntry.description: One interval of a constraint. `to` is `None` while it is in force.

ContentHash.description: SHA-256 of the canonical encoding of a list of operations, as lowercase hex.

DismissRequest.description:
`POST /v1/review/{id}/dismiss`: close a review item without placing its
records.

Dismissal.description:
A reviewer's decision to close a review item without placing its
records.

DocumentEntry.description: One version of a document as the store holds it.

extractions.description: Each time an extractor read this version, oldest first.

length.description: How long the text is, in Unicode code points.

superseded_by.description: The version that replaced this one.

supersedes.description:
The version of the document this one replaced: what the source held
under the same key before.

text.description: The text. Left out of a list of documents.

DocumentExtraction.description: One reading of a document by an extractor.

mentions.description: How many mentions it found in the document.

version.description: The hash of the extractor's files when it ran.

DocumentId.description: Identifies one version of a document. Derived by the engine from the document's source, key and text.

next.description: Pass as `after` for the next page. `null` on the last page.

DocumentsRequest.description:
`POST /v1/documents`: store documents from one source, to be read by an
extractor. The response is the ingest run that stored them.

source.description:
The name of the source the documents come from. The records
extracted from them have the same source.

DraftEntry.description: A draft with the changeset it would commit.

base.description: The log position it was drafted against.

committed_seq.description: Committed: its position in the log.

id.description: The ID of the changeset, which is how a draft is named.

match_run.description: The match run whose judgements the draft rests on.

reconcile_run.description: The reconcile run that drafted it.

rejected_reason.description: Rejected: why, if the reviewer said.

superseded_by.description: Superseded: the reconcile run that drafted the entity type again.

EntityType.description: The name of an entity type the project declares.

rejections.description: With `rejected`: the operations of the changeset that broke a rule.

oneOf.description:
401: nobody is signed in and there is no token, or the username,
password or token is wrong.

403: the caller is known and may not do this: only an admin manages
people, and a write must come from the server's own pages.

429: too many wrong passwords for this username, or more sign-ins
at once than the server checks. Wait and try again.

400: the request cannot be read, or names something that is not
declared.

404: there is no such run, draft, changeset, identity, record,
document, review item or path.
409: the thing exists and is not in a state that allows this.
409: the changeset broke a rule. `rejections` names the operations.
413: the body is larger than the server reads.

500: the project's user code failed, did not finish in time, or
wrote judgements that were refused. The run is recorded as failed
and nothing changed.

500: the project's extractor failed, did not finish in time, or
wrote mentions that were refused. The run is recorded as failed and
nothing it found was stored.
500: the server failed.

ErrorResponse.description: The body of every response that is not a success.

features.description:
Its row in the feature table of its entity type, by column name:
what rules and strategies see of it. `null` when it has no row.

placed.description:
The changeset that put it in the identity it has. `null` while it has
none.

Explanation.description:
What the store knows about a pair of records, and what follows
from it.

comparisons.description: The match runs that looked at the pair, oldest first.

constraints.description:
The constraints between the two, oldest first, with those that were
removed.

left.description: The record with the smaller ID. It is `l` in a rule.

path.description:
When the two share an identity: the shortest chain of links from
`left` to `right` through members of that identity. Empty when they
do not share one, and when no chain joins them as things are now:
what joined them was removed since, or a changeset placed one of
them directly.

review_items.description: The review items that name either of the two, oldest first.

right.description: The record with the larger ID. It is `r` in a rule.

rules.description:
What the project's rules say about the pair now. `null` when the two
are of different entity types, when the engine runs without a
manifest, and when either has no feature row.

summary.description: The explanation in sentences, the outcome first.

duplicates.description:
Mentions that were already known: the same place in the same
document, with the same attributes.

ingest_run.description:
The ingest run the records were stored under. There is none
when nothing was found.

superseded.description:
Records created as a new version of a mention that was known
with other attributes.

ExtractRequest.description:
`POST /v1/extractions`: run one of the project's extractors over the
documents it has not read. The response is the extract run. What it
found is records, which `POST /v1/runs` then matches.

again.description: Read the documents this extractor has read before as well.

extractor.description:
The name of one of the project's extractors; `GET /v1/info` lists
them. The server runs no code it was not built with.

limit.description: Read at most this many documents, oldest first.

source.description: Read only the documents of this source.

wait_ms.description:
How long the call waits for the run, in milliseconds. If the run is
still in progress then, the response has status 202 and the run as
far as it has got.

Extractor.description:
An extractor: a file the engine runs as a child process, which reads
documents and says where they mention entities. The engine runs the file
only while it still has this hash.

file.description:
The file, as a path from the project directory with `/` between its
parts.

hash.description:
SHA-256 of the file and of every file in the directory that shares
its name. It is recorded as the extractor's version with each run.

ExtractorRef.description: Names the extractor of an extract run.

version.description: The hash of the extractor's files.

HistoryEntry.description: A committed changeset as far as it concerns one identity.

ops.description: The operations that name the identity, in the order they were applied.

run.description: The reconcile run that drafted it, if one did.

IdentitiesOfRequest.description:
`POST /v1/records/identities`: the identities of many records
in one call.

identities.description:
One entry per record asked about, in the same order. `null` for
a record that has no identity or is not known.

IdentityId.description: Identifies an identity. Minted once, never derived from content and never reused.

next.description: Pass as `after` for the next page. `null` on the last page.

IdentitySummary.description: An active identity in a list.

label.description:
What a person would call it: the label most of its members have. Of
labels that as many have, the one that was ingested first. `None`
when no member's payload names it. An identity with very many
members is judged by the hundred that were ingested first.

sources.description: The sources its members came from, the one with most members first.

IdentityView.description: An identity and the records that belong to it now.

created.description: The log position that created the identity that was asked for.

current.description:
The active identity it stands for: itself, or the one it was merged
into.

id.description: The ID that was asked for.

label.description:
What a person would call the current identity: the label most of its
members have. `None` when no member's payload names it.

members.description: The members of the current identity, ordered by record ID.

api.description: The version of the API this server speaks.

committed.description: The changeset that put them back, if any went back.

duplicates.description: Rows that were already known, or repeated within this call.

possible_splits.description:
Identities a record went back to where nothing holds it with the
records that are there: what joined them went through a record that
is still taken back. Each has an open `possible_split` review item,
which this run raised.

restored.description:
Records the source had taken back and holds again: every version
of a row that was sent again, changed or not.

returned.description:
Those of them that are back in the identity they left, or in the
one that stands for it now. The rest had none, or can no longer be
there, and are new to the next match run.

superseded.description:
Records created as a new version of a row the source had sent
before under the same key with other content.

IngestRequest.description:
`POST /v1/ingest` with a JSON body. With an Arrow body, the same fields
other than `rows` are query parameters.

rows.description:
One object per row, with the columns the source declares. A column
holds text, booleans or numbers.

source.description:
The name of the source the rows come from, which the project
declares in `sources/<name>.yaml`.

detail.description: Anything the strategy wants kept with the judgement.

score.description:
On the strategy's own scale. Scores are never compared across
strategies.

Link.description: One step in the chain that joins two members of an identity.

run.description: With `match`: the latest run that judged so.

LinkKind.description: What joins two records of one identity directly.

oneOf.description: A `must_link` constraint in force.

One is a later version of the other: the same row of the same
source, sent again with other content.
A run that finished judged them `match`.

LogEntry.description: A committed changeset as the log holds it.

since.description: The log position that placed it here.

MintRequest.description: `POST /v1/ids`: IDs for a caller that writes its own changeset.

MintedIds.description: IDs minted for a caller that writes its own changesets.

NewDocument.description: A document as a source hands it over.

key.description: The document's key within its source: a path, a URL, a message ID.

text.description:
The document as text. Turning a PDF or a web page into text is the
caller's work.

uri.description:
Where the source keeps the document, if that is worth showing to
someone who reads a mention.

Op.description:
One change to identity state. Each operation carries its own precondition,
which is checked against the state the changeset is committed to.

There is no operation that splits an identity. A split is a
`CreateIdentity` and the `Assign` operations that move records to it,
usually with a `cannot_link` constraint, in one changeset.

oneOf.description: Precondition: the ID has never been used.

Attach (`from` is `None`), move, or detach (`to` is `None`).
Precondition: `from` is the record's current identity.

Moves every current member of `from` to `into`, and makes `from` stand
for `into` from then on. Precondition: both are active identities of
one entity type, and no changeset after the author's `base` changed
the members of either. A merge moves every member, and its author saw
only the members there were then.

Records that two records must share an identity, or must not.
Precondition: the pair has no constraint yet, and the state the
changeset leaves behind satisfies this one.
Precondition: the constraint is in force.

Makes a merged identity active again, with no members. It is how a
merge is undone: the changeset that reinstates an identity usually
moves its former members back.

Outcome.description: Where the two records are in relation to each other.

oneOf.description: At least one of the two has no identity.
The two are of different entity types, and are never compared.

PairJudgement.description:
What a run judged about one of a review item's records and another
record.

detail.description:
What the strategy kept with the judgement. The built-in `rules`
keeps the names of the rules that held.

identity.description:
The identity `other` belongs to now: one of the candidates, unless
`other` is another of the item's records, or a record that was
taken back, which has none. A candidate's members
are not all in the case, so this, not the members, says which
candidate a judgement is about.

Person.description:
Someone with an account on this server. The log names a person by `id`,
as `user:<id>`.

active.description: May sign in. An account that is turned off keeps its name in the log.

admin.description: May add people and change their accounts.

email.description:
The address of the Google account they sign in with, where the
server signs people in with Google. `null` for someone who signs in
with a password only.

password.description:
Has a password to sign in with. Someone who has none signs in with
Google.

PersonList.description: `GET /v1/people`: everyone with an account, in the order they were added.

Placement.description: The changeset that put a record where it is.

run.description: The reconcile run that drafted the changeset, if one did.

ReconcileRequest.description: `POST /v1/runs/{run}/reconcile`. The body may be left out.

commit.description: Commit the draft (the default), or store it for review.

RecordEntry.description: A record as it was ingested, and the identity it belongs to now.

evidence.description: Where in the source the record was found, if the source said.

identity.description: `None` while no changeset has placed it.

key.description: The row's key within its source, if it had one.

label.description:
What a person would call it: its value of the feature its type
names as the label. `None` when the type names none, or the record
has no value there.

retracted.description:
The retract run in which its source took the row back, while that
stands. Such a record has no identity and is given none.

superseded_by.description:
The version that replaced this one, if the source has sent the row
again with other content.

supersedes.description:
The version of the row this one replaced: what the source held under
the same key before.

RecordId.description: Identifies a record. Derived by the engine from the record's source, key and content.

next.description: Pass as `after` for the next page. `null` on the last page.

RecordedJudgement.description: A judgement as a run stored it.

detail.description:
What the strategy kept with the judgement. The built-in `rules`
keeps the names of the rules that held.

RejectDraftRequest.description: `POST /v1/drafts/{draft}/reject`. The body may be left out.

Rejection.description:
Why a changeset was not accepted. `op_index` and `op` name the operation
that conflicted, and are `None` when the changeset as a whole is at fault.

committed.description: The changeset that detached them. `None` when none had an identity.

possible_splits.description:
Identities the records left whose remaining members nothing holds
together any more, and that this run raised a `possible_split`
review item for. One that already had an open item keeps it, and
is not counted.

received.description: Keys named, counting a key that was named twice once.

retracted.description:
Records taken back: every version of each row. A record that was
already taken back is not counted again.

unknown.description: Keys under which the source has no row of the entity type.

RetractRequest.description:
`POST /v1/retract`: take back rows a source no longer holds. The
response is the retract run, whose `retraction` says what it did.

Every version of each row stays as evidence and leaves its identity, by
a changeset recorded under the caller. No run examines the records
after that, until an ingest sends a row under the same key again.

keys.description:
The keys of the rows, as the source's key column gave them. A key
the source has no row under is counted as unknown and changes
nothing.

reason.description:
Why, for the log. It is the reason of the changeset that detaches
the records.

source.description: The name of the source that held the rows.

ReviewCase.description:
A review item with what a reviewer reads to decide it: the records
it holds back, the identities they matched, what was judged between
them, and what was already decided about them.

candidates.description:
The identities the item names, as they stand now, ordered by ID. One
that was merged away since is shown as the identity that stands for
it, so there may be fewer than the item names.

constraints.description:
The constraints in force that bear on the decision, oldest first:
those that name one of the item's records, and those between
members of two of the candidates. A changeset that would break one
is refused, so a `cannot_link` between two candidates means they
cannot be merged, and one between a record and a member of a
candidate means it cannot be placed there.

judgements.description:
What the latest run to judge each pair made of it, for every pair of
one of the item's records with another of them, with a member
of a candidate, or with a record in `taken_back`. Only runs that
were reconciled count.

records.description:
The records the item names, as they are now, in the item's
order. One with `retracted` set was taken back by its source: it
does not wait for a decision, and a changeset that gives it an
identity is refused. The decision is about the others.

taken_back.description:
Only a `possible_split` has these: the records that were taken out
of the identity when their source took them back, and have not come
back. What held the groups together went through them, and
`judgements` has what was judged between them and the item's
records.

ReviewEntry.description: A review item as the store keeps it.

dismissed.description: Dismissed: who closed it, when and why.

groups.description:
Only a `possible_split` has these: the records of its identity as
the groups that are each still held together. Nothing the store
knows says that two of the groups are one thing. While the item is
open they are the identity's records as they are now; once it is
closed, as they were last. The largest group is first.

identities.description:
The identities they matched. Empty when the conflict is among the
records themselves. For a `possible_split`, the one identity the
records are in. While the item is open that is the identity as it is
now: when the identity is merged into another, the item names the
one that stands for both.

records.description:
The records left without an identity. For a `possible_split`, the
members of the identity that nothing holds together: every record
in `groups`.

resolved_seq.description:
Resolved: the changeset after which every record had an identity.
For a `possible_split`, the changeset after which nothing was left
to ask: it took the groups apart, or it added what holds them
together, or it merged the identity with one whose item asks for
both.

run.description:
The run that raised it: a reconcile run. For a `possible_split`, the
retract run that took back what held the records together, or the
ingest run that brought a record back to where what held it is
still gone.

superseded_by.description:
Superseded: the reconcile run that raised it again in another form,
or the retract run that took back the records it asked about. For a
`possible_split`, the reconcile run whose judgements hold the
groups together.

ReviewItem.description:
Something the reconciler would not decide. The records named are left
without an identity.

oneOf.description:
The records match members of more than one identity. Those
identities may be the same real thing, which only a reviewer can say.

The evidence contradicts itself: the records match each other or
`identity`, and a `no_match` judgement says some of them do not belong
together, or do not belong with a member of `identity`.

The records match more than one identity, so placing them would
merge identities.
The evidence about the records contradicts itself.

The records share an identity, and nothing the store knows holds
them together any more: what did was a record its source took back.
They may be more than one thing.

RuleReading.description: The project's rules applied to a pair as it is now.

candidate.description:
Whether a block rule holds, so that a run of the rules would compare
the two.

failed.description:
What SQL said when it refused to apply the `no_match` and `match`
rules to the pair, as it refuses the cast of a value that does not
convert. Their `holds` is then `null`. A run applies those rules
only to pairs a block rule found, so a rule may rely on what the
block rules let through and fail on a pair they did not. On a
candidate pair, a run of the rules fails the same way.

verdict.description:
What a run of the rules would judge. `null` when the pair is not a
candidate, and when no `no_match` or `match` rule holds.

RuleResult.description: One rule applied to a pair.

holds.description:
Whether the predicate holds. `null` when it cannot be decided, which
is what SQL makes of a comparison with a feature that is null, and
for a `no_match` or `match` rule when those `failed`. A rule that
cannot be decided does not hold.

predicate.description: The rule's SQL, over the feature rows `l` and `r`.

RunEntry.description: A run as a caller sees it.

entity_type.description: The entity type an ingest, a match or a retract run is about.

extraction.description: What an extract run reported when it finished.

extractor.description:
The extractor of an extract run, and of the ingest run that stored
what it found.

ingest.description:
What an ingest run reported when it finished. The run stored rows,
documents, or the mentions an extract run found.

resolution.description:
What a match run reported when it was reconciled. `committed` is
filled in once its draft is committed.

retraction.description: What a retract run reported when it finished.

strategy.description: The strategy of a match run.

RunId.description: Identifies a run of the engine: an ingest, a match or a reconcile.

RunResponse.description:
A run, as the response of a call that started one or read one. `run` is
`null` when there was nothing to do, so no run was started.

RunStatus.description:
How far a run has got.

Only `running` means the engine is at work. An `open` or `drafted` match
run waits for someone else, and stays as it is across a restart. A run
found `running` when a store is opened was interrupted, and is recorded as
`failed`.

oneOf.description: The engine is working on it.

A match run whose candidates are ready. It takes judgements until it
is reconciled.

A match run that was reconciled into a draft that has not been
committed. The draft's own status says what became of it.

Finished. For a match run: its draft was committed, or there was
nothing to commit.
It stopped with an error, was interrupted, or was cancelled.

Runtime.description: What runs a strategy file. The file's extension decides.

oneOf.description: A `.py` file, run with `uv run`.
A `.ts` file, run with `bun run`.

Seq.description:
A position in the changeset log. The first committed changeset is 1, and 0
is the empty log.

SessionState.description: `GET /auth/session`: who the caller is signed in as.

dev.description:
A development server: nobody signs in, and whoever opens it is the
`dev` account.

google.description:
The server signs people in with Google: `GET /auth/google` in a
browser starts it.

setup.description:
No admin can sign in yet. The server printed a link when it started
that makes the first account.

SetupRequest.description:
`POST /auth/setup`: make the first account, an admin, with the code from
the link the server printed.

SourceCount.description: How many records a source gave.

SourceInfo.description: What one source gave of an entity type.

last_ingested_at.description: When the latest of them was ingested.

records.description: Counting each version of a row.

retracted.description: Those of them the source took back.

unassigned.description: Those of them that wait for an identity.

kept.description: The identity that was split. It keeps its ID and the larger side.

moved.description: The records that moved to the new identity, in order.

base.description:
The log position the identity was read at. With it, the split is
refused if the identity's members changed after that: which side
moves depends on all of them. Without it, the split is made of the
members the identity has now.

keep_apart.description:
Record a `cannot_link` constraint between the two sides (the
default), so that nothing puts them back together unnoticed.

records.description:
The records on one side. The rest of the identity's members are
the other side. The larger side keeps the ID, the side not named here
on a tie.

StartRunRequest.description: `POST /v1/runs`: match the new records of one entity type.

commit.description:
With a strategy the server runs: commit the draft (the default), or
store it for review. A run that waits for judgements is told this
when it is reconciled.

rematch.description:
Match every record of the type again, not only the new ones.
Records that have an identity keep it: where the strategy
disagrees with the identities as they are, the run's `resolution`
lists `suggestions`.

strategy.description:
Who judges. Left out, or named `rules`, the server runs the
project's SQL rules and reconciles. The name of one of the project's
user-code strategies runs that code on the server and reconciles;
`GET /v1/info` lists them. Any other name starts a run that waits
for the caller's judgements: the server runs no code it was not
built with, whatever is named here.

A `version` given with a project strategy must be the hash the
project was built with.

wait_ms.description:
How long the call waits for the run, in milliseconds. If the run is
still in progress then, the response has status 202 and the run as
far as it has got.

extractors.description:
The project's extractors. Empty when the engine runs without a
manifest.

head.description: The position of the last committed changeset.

manifest_hash.description: The hash of the manifest the store was last applied with.

Strategy.description:
A strategy that is user code: a file the engine runs as a child process.
The engine runs the file only while it still has this hash.

file.description:
The file, as a path from the project directory with `/` between its
parts.

hash.description:
SHA-256 of the file and of every file in the directory that shares
its name. It is recorded as the strategy's version with each run.

StrategyRef.description: Names the strategy that produces a match run's judgements.

identities.description: The two identities, the smaller ID first.

matches.description: Pairs of their members the strategy judged `match`.

no_matches.description:
Pairs of their members the strategy judged `no_match`. More than
none means the strategy contradicts itself about these two.

matches.description: Pairs of its members the strategy judged `match`.

no_matches.description: Pairs of its members the strategy judged `no_match`.

Suggestions.description:
What a rematch would change about existing identities if judgements were
allowed to. Nothing here was applied: a reviewer who agrees merges or
splits with a changeset.

merges.description:
Pairs of identities with a `match` between their members, ordered by
their IDs.

splits.description:
Identities with a `no_match` between two of their members, ordered
by ID.

Token.description:
A token: what a caller that is not a person presents, as
`Authorization: Bearer <token>`. The log names what it changed by the
token's name, as `agent:<name>`.

created_by.description:
The ID of the person who made it. `null` when it was made on the
server's machine with `spool token add`.

last_used_at.description: When it was last presented, to the minute. `null` if it never was.

TokenList.description:
`GET /v1/tokens`: every token, in the order they were made. Only an
admin may read it.

declaration_version.description: How many times the declaration has been applied in a new form.

features.description:
The columns of the feature table, as the manifest declares them.
Empty when the engine runs without a manifest.

open_draft.description: The draft that waits for a decision, if there is one.

retracted.description: Records their source took back. They are counted in `records`.

sources.description: The sources the records came from, by name.

strategies.description:
The project's user-code strategies for the type. The built-in
`rules` is always there and is not listed.

unassigned.description:
Records that wait for an identity: no changeset has placed them,
and their source has not taken them back.

committed.description:
The changeset, once it is committed. `None` when there was nothing to
commit, and while a draft waits.

draft.description:
The draft that was stored for review, if the run was asked to leave
one. It is named by its changeset ID.

new_records.description:
Records the run examined: those ingested since the last run, and
those an earlier run left for review.

records_unassigned.description:
Examined records left without an identity. Each is named in
`review`.

reexamined.description: How many of them an earlier run had left for review.

review.description: What the run would not decide. The store keeps these as review items.

suggestions.description:
Where the strategy disagrees with the identities as they are. Only a
rematch has these: no other run judges pairs of records that
both have an identity.

UndoRequest.description:
`POST /v1/changesets/{seq}/undo`: take back the changeset at a log
position with a new changeset.

commit.description: Commit the undo (the default), or only validate it and return it.
